obligations.note: The new branch in is_allowed grants any 'report:<action>' name whose stripped form is in GRANTS. So pairs outside the approved closed matrix are allowed, for example ('treasury_manager', 'report:release_payment') and ('payments_officer', 'report:approve_payment'). That breaks default-deny for action names not in ACTIONS or the approved access policy, and the exhaustive control test only enumerates declared actions, so it cannot catch this.

The alias resolves only to existing grants, and the auditor's grants (view_account, view_audit, view_reports, export_ledger) include no state-changing action. The exhaustive test_auditor_is_read_only passed on head.
it_admin has no approve_payment or release_payment grant, so the 'report:' alias cannot give it either. The exhaustive test_it_admin_cannot_approve_or_release passed on head.
Ticket CHG-24119 was approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-03, before review. Its components (payments.access) cover the only touched file, rbac.py.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver and not the author Sofia Santos, gave a code_review approval.
Both approvals name the head commit ce0d48fe, and there are no later commits.

run.json records a successful ci/run-tests.sh baseline-payments run on the head commit. The JUnit report shows 172 tests passing with none skipped, including the ACC-1, ACC-2 and SOD-1 control tests. Those tests cannot see the new prefix path, and no unit test was added despite the description's claim.
payments.access is security_sensitive. Ines Halvorsen (security_reviewer) approved a security_review on the head commit.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers rbac.py. The covered code (payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, and the Mortgage Approvals, Underwriting and Policy files) is unchanged.

summary: The change adds a 'report:' prefix to rbac.is_allowed that silently aliases any prefixed action name to the underlying grant. This creates allowed role/action pairs outside the approved, closed access matrix, including privileged and state-changing actions such as approve_payment and release_payment, which violates ACC-1's default-deny and approved-matrix requirement. No exception in the register covers this deviation. Passing control tests do not cure it, because they enumerate only the declared action set. The process records are otherwise in order, but the ACC-1 violation requires rejection.
